JUDGMENT MFA.CROB.No.100023/2022 is filed by the claimants in MFA No.100530/2017 challenging the judgment and award dated 04.10.2016 in M.V.C. No.146/2015 passed by the learned Senior Civil and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kushtagi, for seeking enhancement of compensation whereas MFA Nos.100529/2017 and 100530/2017 are filed by the Insurance Company in M.V.C.
Nos.145/2015 and 146/2015 respectively questioning the liability fixed on the Insurance Company on the ground that the driver of the tractor trailor was not holding driving license.

entities.text: Senior Civil and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kushtagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that on 12.03.2012 at about 2.00 p.m. the deceased Basavaraj and another person were going on TVS motorcycle from Kushtagi Town to Tondihal village.
When they were near Bandi Cross, the tractor-trailer bearing registration No.KA-37/TA-3280, KA-37/TA-2420 was coming from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result of the said accident Hanumantha sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries in the Government Hospital, Kushtagi.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the claimants under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the death of the deceased in the road traffic accident.

4. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties on both sides and perused the records.
5.
In the present case, the accident was occurred in between tractor-trailer and motorcycle.
The learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that driver of tractor was not holding driving license.
Hence, the Insurance Company is not liable to indemnify the owner of tractor and to pay compensation to the claimants.
In the appeal, the counsel for the respondent-owner of the tractor has filed copy of driving license.

This Court by exercising its powers under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code NC: 2023:KHC-D:8852 C/W MFA No. 100529 of 2017, of Civil Procedure, 1908 accepting the said driving license as additional evidence produced in the appeal proving that the tractor driver was holding driving license as on the date of the accident.
Therefore, the said driving license is hereby considered as additional evidence.
Upon perusing of his driving license, the driving license is issued on 18.05.2005 for driving light motor vehicle and it is valid up to 17.05.2025 for driving LMV (non transport).
Then for driving of transport vehicle in the same class of vehicle is with effect from 14.07.2006.
Therefore, the driver has produced driving license to drive light motor vehicle (non- transport) and was having driving license to drive same class of vehicle but the vehicle is different type.
In this regard, the issue involved in no more res integra in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and others1.

sentences.text: Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in fastening the liability on the Insurance Company to indemnify the owner of the tractor trailer and to pay compensation to the claimants.

7. The Tribunal has awarded compensation as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Rs.9,72,000/-
2. Funeral expenses Rs.20,000/-
3. Loss of estate Rs.20,000/-
4. Loss of consortium Rs.20,000/-
In the present case, the deceased was aged 24 years and was an agriculturists and coolie died in the accident caused on 12.03.2012.
The Tribunal has taken the income as Rs.6,000/- which is on lower side.
Therefore, as per chart of notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, a sum of Rs.6,500/- per month to be taken as notional monthly income of the deceased.
The Tribunal has not added NC: 2023:KHC-D:8852 C/W MFA No. 100529 of 2017, income towards loss of future prospects in life.

According to the age of the deceased, 40% of the income is to be added towards 'Loss of Future Prospects' as per the judgment of the Honb'le Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi,2 i.e., Rs.2,600/- (Rs.6,500 x 40%).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi,2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the monthly income of the deceased is taken at Rs.9,100/-.
Since the deceased was a bachelor, 50% of his income is deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

The appropriate multiplier applicable as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma &
Others. Vs.
Delhi Transport Corpn And Another is '18'.

Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss of Dependency along with Loss of Future Prospects in Life' is reassessed and quantified as follows:
Rs.6,500 + Rs.2,600 (40% of Rs.6,500) x 50% x 18 x 12 = 9,82,800/-.
(2017) 16 SCC 680 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8852 C/W MFA No. 100529 of 2017,

There are totally three dependants of the deceased, hence as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited vs. Nanu Ram & Others3 and National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi4

Loss of Dependency along with 1. Rs.9,82,800/-
Loss of Future Prospects in Life 2. Loss of Consortium including Rs.1,20,000/- 2018 ACJ 2782 (2017) 16 SCC 680 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8852 C/W MFA No. 100529 of 2017, Loss of Love and Affection Loss of Transportation of dead 3. Rs.15,000/-
body expenses 4. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
Total Rs.11,32,800/-
12.
The Tribunal has taken interest at 8% per annum and the same is scaled down at 6% per annum.
Therefore, so far as rate of the interest is concerned, the appeal filed by the insurance company is allowed in part.
13. Therefore, the claimants are awarded a total compensation of Rs.11,32,800/- as against the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.10,32,000/-.

Hence, the claimants are entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.1,00,800/- (Rs.11,32,800 - Rs.10,32,000), along with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of filing of the petition till deposit.
However, the claimants are not entitled for interest for the period of 1267 days delay in filing the appeal.

14. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:

3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the claimants under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the death of the deceased in the road traffic accident.
In the present case, the accident was occurred in between tractor-trailer and motorcycle.
The learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that driver of tractor was not holding driving license.
Hence, the Insurance Company is not liable to indemnify the owner of tractor and to pay compensation to the claimants.
This Court by exercising its powers under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code NC: 2023:KHC-D:8852 C/W MFA No. 100529 of 2017, of Civil Procedure, 1908 accepting the said driving license as additional evidence produced in the appeal proving that the tractor driver was holding driving license as on the date of the accident.
Upon perusing of his driving license, the driving license is issued on 18.05.2005 for driving light motor vehicle and it is valid up to 17.05.2025 for driving LMV (non transport).
Then for driving of transport vehicle in the same class of vehicle is with effect from 14.07.2006.
Therefore, the driver has produced driving license to drive light motor vehicle (non- transport) and was having driving license to drive same class of vehicle but the vehicle is different type.
In this regard, the issue involved in no more res integra in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and others1.
Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in fastening the liability on the Insurance Company to indemnify the owner of the tractor trailer and to pay compensation to the claimants.
